fixer.summary: Guidance and Shield of Faith are now marked `default_self=True` in dungdra/data/spells.py. `_guidance` and `_shield_of_faith` no longer fall back to `c.caster` when no target is named; they just use `targets[0]`. So every self-default now comes from the existing `sd["default_self"]` check in `cast()`, which is tagged SRD[SPELL.casting-spells.effects.targets#3]. I added unit tests for three things: the data flag, casting with no target landing on the caster, and a named target taking precedence over the default. The ticket names no acceptance tests. All 774 tests pass, ruff check and format are clean, and dev-gate passes.

findings.explanation: test_self_defaulting_spells_say_so_in_their_data only reads the data flags back. Not a blocker, because the next two tests check the actual behaviour: with no target named, the spell lands on the caster, and a named target overrides that.

review.summary: I approve this fix. Guidance and Shield of Faith now set `default_self=True` in their data, and their handlers no longer fall back to the caster by hand. The self-default is now applied in one place, `cast()` in `dungdra/spells.py`, which also carries the right SRD tag (SPELL.casting-spells.effects.targets#3). Readied release reuses the targets `cast()` already resolved, so taking out the handler fallback doesn't break that path. No other handler still has `targets[0] if targets else c.caster`; the one remaining `if targets else` at spells.py:1459 picks a position for an area spell, which is a separate mechanism. The new unit tests check the behaviour: with no target, the caster gets the effect, and a named target overrides the default. The data-set test on its own is weak but harmless. Nothing in the diff goes beyond the ticket.
